RESERVED ON : NOVEMBER 7th, 2023 PRONOUNCED ON : DECEMBER 11th, 2023 JUDGMENT 1.
Being aggrieved by the judgment and order passed by the Adhoc District Judge - 5, Nagpur in Land Acquisition Case No.73/1995, the appellant has preferred this appeal.
The respondents have filed cross- objection in the said appeal in the year 2023.

2. The first appeal and the cross-objection arise out of the judgment and order dated 03.12.2008 passed by the Adhoc District Judge - 5, Nagpur and, therefore, the same are being disposed of by common judgment.
3.
The appellant is Vidarbha Irrigation Development Corporation (VIDC).

That the appellant has acquired total 3.72 hectares perennial irrigated land along with trees, bunds, pipe lines etc at survey No.117/A situated at mouza Ridhora (Gujar), Tah. Umred, Dist. Nagpur for the construction of Wadgaon Dam under Lower Wanna Project in Land 3/6 FA.429.09-JF.odt Acquisition Case No.46/A-65/1989-90.
The award in this case was passed on 16.03.1995.

Thereafter, the appellant has filed the reference application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act against the award passed in Land Acquisition Case No.46/A-65/1989-90 of mouza Ridhora (Gujar), Tahasil Umred,
District Nagpur.

The reference Court by its judgment dated 03.12.2008 in Land Acquisition Case No.73/1995 enhanced the compensation for 3.72 hectare perennial irrigated land at Survey No.117/A at the rate of Rs.75,000/- per hectare.
4. The notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act was published in official gazette for acquisition of land admeasuring 211.28 hectare.
The respondent No.1 was paid compensation to the tune of Rs.2,08,879/- for the said land including cost of land, trees and solatium and interest before the Collector, Nagpur.
Initially the Ad hoc District Judge partly allowed the reference application and granted huge additional compensation along with solatium and interest.
Since the appellant was not made party before the reference Court, this Court has remanded the matter to fresh disposal as the VIDC was not joined as necessary party to the proceedings.
The Ad hoc District Judge - 5, Nagpur partly allowed the reference application and granted compensation at the rate of Rs.75,000/- per hectare.

sentences.text: The appellant has brought to my notice that the First Appeal No.16/2008 and First Appeal No.54/2015 came to be decided on 18.01.2019 determining the compensation by this Court at the rate of Rs.45,000/- per acre i.e. Rs.1,12,500/- per hectare for dry crop land of mouza Ridhora (Gujar) in respect of land at survey No.114 admeasuring 5.21 hectares, which was acquired for the same project and situated in same village Ridhora (Gujar) and were adjoining to each other having same potential.

6. After going through the judgment in above said Appeal Nos.16/2008 and 54/2015, the respondent No.1 in this appeal came to know that the things attached thereto and the lands were not properly valued by the reference Court because it must be a typographical mistake committed by the reference Court while determining the market value of the perennial irrigated land of the respondent No.1/claimant in cross- objection at the rate of Rs.75,000/- per hectare.

7. This Court in First Appeal Nos.16/2008 and 54/2015 has upheld the market value of the dry crop land of the neighbouring land owner at the rate of Rs.1,12,500/- per hectare, whose land was acquired for the same project, by the same notifications and award.
The appellant is also entitled for double of the market value of dry crop land, his land being the perennial irrigated one on the ground of parity.
The Court has 5/6 FA.429.09-JF.odt determined the value of the land of the dry crop land at the rate of 40,000/- per acre.
However, the acquired land in the present case was perennially irrigated land as there is a well in Khasara No.117/A, there is entry in this respect in 7/12 extract of the land.
However, instead of per acre, the Court has mentioned it as Rs.75,000/- per hectare.

Therefore, in cross-objection, the appellant has raised the objection that the respondents have not valued the irrigated land as per the valuation and instead of stating per acre, it is mentioned as per hectare, which caused injustice to the appellant in cross-objection.

8. Considering the value determined by the reference Court for dry crop land at the rate of 40,000/-
per acre, the value of irrigated land cannot be at the rate of Rs.75,000/- per hectare.

Considering,
the error committed by the Trial Court while determining the value of the irrigated land and considering the First Appeal Nos.16/2008 and 54/2015, I am of the view that the typographical mistake is required to be corrected, however, the reference Court has not committed any error by enhancing the compensation for the land.
9. The present case is covered by the judgment dated 18.01.2019 passed by this Court in First Appeal Nos.16/2008 and 54/2015 as both these lands were acquired from same village and same project.
The compensation towards the value of trees is concerned, the 6/6 FA.429.09-JF.odt reference Court has adopted the same procedure and determined the value of trees.

The enhancement was granted by the reference Court, therefore, cannot said to be exorbitant but as per the cross-objection, it is required to be corrected as the determination of dry crop land and determination of the irrigated land is not properly valued.
Therefore, the error in granting the enhanced compensation for irrigated land is required to be corrected as Rs.75,000/- per acre instead of per hectare.

Hence, the appeal stands dismissed and the cross-objection is partly allowed by correcting the determination of valuation by Rs.75,000/- per acre instead of Rs. 75,000/-per V.I.D.C. Thr. Exe.
